seo_title: Solar Lead Generation in Delhi: Targeting by DISCOM Area
description: Solar lead generation in Delhi after the 2026 free rooftop solar route: target by DISCOM area, filter by monthly units and book more paid site visits.
headline: Solar lead generation in Delhi: how targeting changes by DISCOM area
card_text: Delhi's 2026 free rooftop solar route changed who pays an installer. How to target by DISCOM area, filter leads by monthly units and keep your site visits worth the trip.
intro:
Solar lead generation in Delhi is not the same job it was a year ago. Since the Delhi Solar Energy Policy's second amendment in September 2026, many smaller households can get a 2–3 kW rooftop system through a government-run route with little or nothing to pay. That is good news for Delhi, but it means a lot of the cheap enquiries your ads attract are from people who will never sign a private installer's quote.

This guide is for installers and EPCs selling rooftop solar inside Delhi. It covers what the new rules mean for your targeting, how the five power distribution areas in the city differ, how to filter leads by monthly units, and which channels bring in the paying customers that are left: bigger homes, larger systems, housing societies and commercial roofs.

sections.h2: What the 2026 Delhi solar rules mean for your leads
sections.html:
Here is the short version, as reported in late 2026. Always check the current rules on the Delhi Solar Portal and the PM Surya Ghar portal before you put any figure in an ad.

  • Two routes now exist. A government-led route (described as a DISCOM trusteeship or utility-led aggregation model) where vendors are picked by tender and households up to 3 kW pay little or nothing. And an open route, where the household picks a registered vendor and agrees a price.
  • Eligibility for the free route depends on consumption. Published guidance ties it to average monthly consumption in the last financial year, with the cut-off at around 400 units a month. Homes above that line, or wanting more than 3 kW, go through the open route.
  • The state subsidy is higher than before. Reports of the amendment put it at up to ₹26,000 per kW for the first 3 kW, capped at ₹78,000, on top of the central PM Surya Ghar subsidy, with the total limited to the project cost.

For your marketing, the takeaway is simple: monthly units is now your most important qualifying question in Delhi. A household using 250 units a month may be better off on the free route. A household using 700 units, running two or three ACs through summer, needs a bigger system and a vendor it trusts. That second household is your customer.

sections.h2: Delhi's DISCOM areas and how targeting differs
sections.html:
Delhi is not one market. Five bodies distribute power in the city, and each area has a different mix of housing, roof access and buyers. Your ad sets, landing pages and sales scripts should reflect that.

DISCOMBroad areaWhat the lead pool tends to look like
BSES Rajdhani (BRPL)South and west DelhiIndependent houses, kothis and builder floors with high summer loads. Bigger systems, more site visits, premium buyers who compare brands.
BSES Yamuna (BYPL)East and central DelhiDense colonies and smaller roofs. Many households fall near or under the free-route cut-off, so filtering by units matters most here.
Tata Power-DDL (TPDDL)North and north-west DelhiA mix of plotted colonies, DDA flats and industrial areas, which gives you both residential and small commercial leads.
NDMCNew Delhi (Lutyens' zone)Small, high-value pool: bungalows and institutional buildings. Fewer leads, longer conversations.
MESDelhi CantonmentDefence housing with its own approvals. Usually not worth a separate campaign.

A practical setup is one campaign per DISCOM group, targeted by pincode, with the DISCOM named in the ad and on the page. "Rooftop solar for BSES Rajdhani homes in Dwarka and Janakpuri" tells a homeowner you know their paperwork. It also lets you see which area gives you the cheapest paid site visit, not just the cheapest form fill.

sections.h2: Qualifying questions for solar lead generation in Delhi
sections.html:
Your lead form or WhatsApp auto-reply should do the filtering before a salesperson spends a call on it. For Delhi, ask:

  1. Average monthly units (from the electricity bill): under 400, 400–700, 700–1,000, above 1,000. This is the question the 2026 rules made essential.
  2. Your DISCOM: BSES Rajdhani, BSES Yamuna, Tata Power-DDL, NDMC or not sure.
  3. Do you own the roof? Owner of the whole house, owner of the top floor, tenant, or housing society. Builder floors in Delhi often have shared roofs, and that has to come up before the site visit, not during it.
  4. Locality or pincode, so you can route the lead to the right team.
  5. When do you want it installed? This month, in the next three months, just exploring.

Leads under 400 units are not worthless. Be honest with them: explain the free route, offer to help if they want a larger or branded system, and ask for a referral. Being the installer who told them the truth is how a Delhi colony starts recommending you.

sections.h2: Channels that work for Delhi installers
sections.html:
The channels themselves are familiar. What changes in Delhi is how you set them up.

  • Google Search: people searching "solar panel installation in Rohini" or "rooftop solar BSES net metering" are already deciding. Build ad groups by area and by intent (cost, subsidy, net metering, brand). Add negatives such as "free solar scheme registration", "job" and "dealership" so you don't pay for searches that will never become paid installs. Our Google Ads guide for solar companies covers the full keyword structure.
  • Meta lead ads and click-to-WhatsApp: best for volume. Use the qualifying questions above, show real installations from the same part of Delhi, and lead with bill savings on larger systems rather than "free solar" claims. The Facebook ads setup guide has the form and creative details.
  • Google Business Profile: Delhi homeowners search "solar company near me" and check reviews before they call back. A profile with recent reviews and photos tagged by colony helps every other channel convert.
  • RWAs and housing societies: group housing societies have their own subsidy track under the policy. A talk at an RWA meeting or a common-area proposal can bring in many households at once, though it takes longer.
  • Referrals from finished jobs: neighbours watch installations happen. A site board and a short walk-through video shared in the colony WhatsApp group often outperform paid ads for cost per order.

sections.h2: How to talk about subsidies without misleading anyone
sections.html:
Delhi buyers now hear about "free solar" from the news, the DISCOM and their neighbours. If your ad promises the same thing and your quote doesn't match, you lose trust and may be breaking ad platform rules on misleading claims.

  • Say "you may be eligible for central and Delhi government subsidies" and link to the official portals, rather than stating a fixed rupee amount as guaranteed.
  • Put any figures on your landing page with the date you checked them and a line telling people to confirm on the official portal.
  • Explain the difference between the free route and the open route in one plain sentence, and say who each suits.
  • Sell what the open route actually gives a buyer: system size matched to their load, brand choice, and a named installer responsible for service.

Our guide on using the PM Surya Ghar subsidy in ads goes deeper on wording that stays accurate when rules change.

sections.h2: What to measure and what to expect
sections.html:
In Delhi, cost per lead will mislead you more than anywhere else in NCR, because the cheapest leads are often households that qualify for the free route. Track these instead, by DISCOM area:

  • Share of leads above 400 units a month
  • Leads that pick up and confirm they own the roof
  • Site visits booked and done
  • Quotes sent, orders won and average system size

For context, Performance and Pixel's rooftop solar campaigns typically land at ₹60–80 per qualified enquiry, and solar clients at scale typically get 20–30 leads a day and 5–10 site visits a week. Your numbers will depend on your area, offer, reviews and how fast your team calls back, and no agency can honestly guarantee them. What you can control is making sure each site visit is with someone who can actually become a paying customer.

sections.h2: A simple 30-day plan for a Delhi installer
sections.html:
1. Week 1: list the pincodes your team can cover, group them by DISCOM, update your Google Business Profile and add the units question to every form.
  2. Week 2: launch Google Search for two or three areas and one Meta lead campaign per DISCOM group, with installation photos from those areas.
  3. Week 3: call every lead within minutes, log units, roof ownership and outcome in one sheet, and pause areas where few leads are above 400 units.
  4. Week 4: move budget to the areas with the lowest cost per site visit done, and start asking finished customers for reviews and referrals.

faqs: How do solar installers get leads in Delhi?

Most Delhi installers combine Google Search ads by locality, Meta lead ads or click-to-WhatsApp ads with qualifying questions, a well-reviewed Google Business Profile, RWA outreach and referrals from finished installations. The key in 2026 is filtering by monthly units so you focus on homes that need the open route.
Is rooftop solar free in Delhi now?

Under the 2026 amendment to the Delhi Solar Energy Policy, eligible residential consumers with lower monthly consumption can get a 2–3 kW system through a government-led route at little or no cost. Eligibility depends on past consumption and other conditions, so check the Delhi Solar Portal for the current rules.
Which DISCOM areas are best for solar leads in Delhi?

It depends on your offer. BSES Rajdhani areas in south and west Delhi have many independent houses with high loads, which suits larger systems. Tata Power-DDL areas in the north mix homes and small commercial roofs. BSES Yamuna areas are denser, so lead filtering matters more there.
What should a solar lead form ask in Delhi?
Ask for average monthly units, DISCOM, roof ownership, locality or pincode and installation timeline. These five answers tell your team whether a site visit is worth booking.
Can I advertise the Delhi solar subsidy amount in my ads?

You can mention that subsidies may be available, but avoid presenting a rupee amount as guaranteed. Put dated figures on your landing page and point people to the official Delhi Solar Portal and PM Surya Ghar portal to confirm.
